meta.label: E-readers
tradeoffLabels: reads open formats and library books
meta.attribution: Options are e-reader models on sale in October 2026: Amazon Kindle (US, UK, EU), Rakuten Kobo (sold widely), PocketBook (EU) and BOOX e-ink Android tablets (US, EU). Open formats: from each maker's own format and library pages; 85 to 92 for readers that open EPUB and Adobe DRM books from any shop natively or run any reading app, plus built-in library borrowing; 35 for Kindles, which take EPUB only through Amazon's Send to Kindle conversion and borrow library books only in the US. Reading privacy: from what each maker publishes about data its e-readers send; 30 where the terms list reading position, viewing data and search queries (Amazon), 40 where an account is required and usage data is used for personalization (Kobo); left blank where the maker publishes nothing specific to the device (PocketBook, BOOX), because unknown is not zero. Long support: the maker's published security update period, about four years for Amazon and Kobo (62), plus 16 points where official replacement batteries and screens are sold (Kobo's iFixit programme, 78); BOOX devices run Android and carry an EU tablet label, scored from the years of updates declared there as in the tablets lens (5 years 70, 7 years 90). PocketBook publishes no support period, so that cell is blank. Price: the maker's own store on the date checked, in its currency, at face value (150 or less scores 95, up to 200 scores 88, 300 scores 80, 400 scores 72, 500 scores 64, 650 scores 56). Not scored: screen quality and store catalogue size. Left out: reMarkable, a note-taking tablet with no bookstore and no DRM book support; Barnes & Noble Nook and tolino, whose maker pages could not be read for this review. Sources: Amazon help and Kindle terms, Libby help, Kobo help centre, iFixit's Kobo repair hub, PocketBook spec pages and store, BOOX store, the EU product register (EPREL). Reviewed 2026-10. Suggest changes via Contribute.

criteria.label: Reading data sent to the maker

products.name: Amazon Kindle (2026)
products.description: Amazon's 2026 basic 6-inch Kindle, the cheapest new e-reader here, tied to Amazon's store and formats.

openness.note: Kindles do not open EPUB files copied over directly; Amazon's Send to Kindle service accepts EPUB, PDF and a few document types and converts them for the device, DRM-free files only.

privacy.note: Amazon's Kindle Store terms say Kindle software sends Amazon information about how you use it, 'such as your last page read', the content you use or archive, your viewing data and search queries.

longevity.note: Amazon's Kindle security page lists 'Kindle (2026 Release), 16GB' as getting security updates at least through 31 December 2030, or four years from purchase from Amazon if later. Amazon sells no spare parts for Kindles.

economical.note: Amazon's Kindle e-reader page lists the 2026 Kindle (16 GB) at $149.99; a 32 GB aluminium version without lockscreen ads is $189.99.

products.name: Amazon Kindle Paperwhite (2026)
products.description: The 2026 waterproof 7-inch Paperwhite, the mainstream e-reader most people compare against.

openness.note: On the Kindle Paperwhite (2026), library books come only through Libby's Send to Kindle route, which Libby says is 'available in the U.S. only'; elsewhere Kindles cannot borrow from OverDrive libraries.

privacy.note: Under Amazon's Kindle Store terms the Kindle Paperwhite (2026) reports reading activity to Amazon, including last page read, viewing data and search queries; buying and borrowing need an Amazon account.

longevity.note: Amazon's Kindle security update table lists the Kindle Paperwhite (2026 Release) as supported at least through 31 December 2030, or four years from purchase from Amazon; there is no official battery or parts programme.

economical.note: Amazon's Kindle e-reader page lists the 2026 Kindle Paperwhite (16 GB) at $199.99.

products.name: Amazon Kindle Paperwhite Signature Edition (2026)
products.description: The Paperwhite with an aluminium back, 32 GB and an auto-adjusting light.

openness.note: Amazon's Send to Kindle help lists EPUB among accepted files, but the Kindle Paperwhite Signature Edition (2026) reads them only after Amazon's cloud conversion; books bought elsewhere with Adobe DRM cannot be read.

privacy.note: The same Kindle Store terms apply to the Signature Edition: reading position, viewing data and searches are sent to Amazon.

longevity.note: Amazon's Kindle security update table lists the Kindle Paperwhite Signature Edition (2026 Release) as supported at least through 31 December 2030, or four years from purchase from Amazon; there is no official battery or parts programme.

economical.note: Amazon's Kindle e-reader page lists the 2026 Paperwhite Signature Edition (32 GB) at $249.99.

products.name: Amazon Kindle Colorsoft (2026)
products.description: Amazon's colour e-ink Kindle, redesigned in 2026, for comics, covers and picture books.

openness.note: The Kindle Colorsoft (2026) reads Amazon's own formats; EPUB arrives only through Send to Kindle, and Libby library loans reach Kindles in the US only.

privacy.note: Amazon's Kindle Store terms list last page read, content use, viewing data and search queries among what Kindle software sends to Amazon, which covers the Colorsoft too.

longevity.note: Amazon's Kindle security update table lists the Kindle Colorsoft (2026 Release) as supported at least through 31 December 2030, or four years from purchase from Amazon; there is no official battery or parts programme.

economical.note: Amazon's Kindle e-reader page lists the 2026 Kindle Colorsoft (16 GB) at $289.99, or $319.99 for the Signature Edition.

products.name: Amazon Kindle Scribe (3rd generation)
products.description: Amazon's 11-inch writing e-reader with a pen; a version without front light is cheaper.

openness.note: The Scribe shares the Kindle file rules: EPUB only via Amazon's Send to Kindle conversion and Libby loans in the US only, though PDFs can be annotated with the pen.

privacy.note: The Kindle Store terms cover the Scribe; notes and documents synced to the account add to what Amazon holds beyond reading position and searches.

longevity.note: Amazon's Kindle security update table lists the Kindle Scribe Generation 3 as supported at least through 31 December 2030, or four years from purchase from Amazon; there is no official battery or parts programme.

economical.note: Amazon's Kindle e-reader page lists the Kindle Scribe (32 GB) at $499.99 and the Scribe without front light (16 GB) at $429.99.

products.name: Amazon Kindle Scribe Colorsoft
products.description: The colour version of the Scribe, the most expensive e-reader here.

openness.note: The Scribe Colorsoft follows the same Kindle rules: no direct EPUB, Send to Kindle conversion for DRM-free files, Libby loans in the US only.

privacy.note: Kindle Store terms apply: Amazon receives reading position, viewing data and search queries from the Scribe Colorsoft.

longevity.note: Amazon's Kindle security update table lists the Kindle Scribe Colorsoft Generation 1 as supported at least through 31 December 2030, or four years from purchase from Amazon; there is no official battery or parts programme.

economical.note: Amazon's Kindle e-reader page lists the Kindle Scribe Colorsoft (32 GB) at $629.99.

products.name: Kobo Clara BW
products.description: A 6-inch e-reader that reads EPUB natively and borrows library books directly; official repair parts through iFixit.

openness.note: Kobo's format help lists EPUB, EPUB2, EPUB3, PDF, MOBI and CBZ/CBR comics for its e-readers and says 'Your eReader supports Adobe DRM and Social DRM.', so books from most non-Amazon shops open.

privacy.note: Kobo's setup help says 'To sign in to your eReader, you’ll need a Kobo account.', and Kobo's separate privacy settings page says it may process information about your use to personalize your reading experience and recommendations.

longevity.note: Kobo commits to security updates for the Kobo Clara BW until at least 31 December 2028 for UK sales and, globally, 'software security updates for at least a period of four years' after a model was last sold; iFixit's Kobo repair hub sells official Clara BW parts, including batteries and screens, with guides.

economical.note: Kobo's US e-reader store lists the Kobo Clara BW at $159.99.

products.name: Kobo Clara Colour
products.description: The colour 6-inch Kobo, with the same open formats, library borrowing and official parts as the Clara BW.

openness.note: Kobo says the built-in Libby by OverDrive feature on the Kobo Clara Colour lets owners borrow from public libraries in Canada, the US, the UK, Australia, New Zealand, the Nordics and parts of Asia.

privacy.note: Setting up the Clara Colour needs a Kobo account, and Kobo says it may use information about your use of its service to personalize recommendations and emails.

longevity.note: Kobo commits to security updates for the Kobo Clara Colour until at least 31 December 2028 for UK sales and, globally, 'software security updates for at least a period of four years' after a model was last sold; iFixit's Kobo repair hub sells official Clara Colour parts, including batteries and screens, with guides.

economical.note: Kobo's US e-reader store lists the Kobo Clara Colour at $179.99.

products.name: Kobo Libra Colour
products.description: A 7-inch colour Kobo with page-turn buttons and stylus support, covered by Kobo's iFixit parts programme.

openness.note: The Kobo Libra Colour is on Kobo's list of e-readers with built-in Libby library borrowing, and Kobo's format help lists native EPUB3, PDF and comic formats with Adobe DRM support.

privacy.note: Kobo requires an account to sign in on its e-readers and describes using service data to personalize reading, recommendations and pages; Kobo's full privacy policy could not be opened from here.

longevity.note: Kobo commits to security updates for the Kobo Libra Colour until at least 31 December 2028 for UK sales and, globally, 'software security updates for at least a period of four years' after a model was last sold; iFixit's Kobo repair hub sells official Libra Colour parts, including batteries and screens, with guides.

economical.note: Kobo's US e-reader store lists the Kobo Libra Colour at $259.99.

products.name: Kobo Sage
products.description: An 8-inch Kobo from 2021, still sold, with open formats and library borrowing but no official parts kit.

openness.note: Kobo lists the Sage among e-readers with built-in Libby by OverDrive borrowing, in countries including the US, UK and Canada; EPUB and Adobe DRM books from other shops open too.

privacy.note: The Sage, like every Kobo, asks for a Kobo account at setup; Kobo's published privacy settings describe personalization from usage data.

longevity.note: Kobo's security policy lists the Kobo Sage as getting security updates until 31 December 2028 under its UK commitment, plus at least four years after the model was last sold; iFixit's Kobo repair hub does not list parts for it.

economical.note: Kobo's US e-reader store lists the Kobo Sage at $269.99.

products.name: Kobo Elipsa 2E
products.description: Kobo's 10.3-inch writing e-reader with stylus included; open formats, but no official parts.

openness.note: The Elipsa 2E reads EPUB, PDF and comic files natively, supports Adobe DRM and Social DRM, and borrows from libraries through Kobo's built-in Libby feature where available.

privacy.note: The Elipsa 2E needs a Kobo account to set up, and notebooks sync through Kobo's services; Kobo describes personalizing content from usage information.

longevity.note: Kobo's security policy lists the Kobo Elipsa 2E as getting security updates until 31 December 2028 under its UK commitment, plus at least four years after the model was last sold; iFixit's Kobo repair hub does not list parts for it.

economical.note: Kobo's US e-reader store lists the Kobo Elipsa 2E at $399.99.

products.name: PocketBook Verse
products.description: PocketBook's cheapest 6-inch reader, with no store lock-in and the widest native format list here.

openness.note: PocketBook's spec page for the Verse lists 21 book formats read without conversion, including EPUB and PDF with Adobe DRM, MOBI, AZW3, FB2, DJVU and CBZ, so library and shop books from outside Amazon open directly.

economical.note: PocketBook's German store lists the PocketBook Verse at 135 euros including VAT.

products.name: PocketBook Verse Pro
products.description: A waterproof 6-inch PocketBook with page buttons and an audiobook player.

openness.note: The Verse Pro spec page advertises '25 formats support, including Adobe DRM technology', listing EPUB and PDF with DRM, MOBI, AZW3, FB2 and DJVU among the book formats read without conversion.

economical.note: PocketBook's German store lists the PocketBook Verse Pro at 169 euros including VAT.

products.name: PocketBook Era Color
products.description: A 7-inch colour PocketBook with page-turn buttons.

openness.note: PocketBook's Era Color spec lists EPUB and PDF with Adobe DRM, MOBI, AZW3, DJVU, FB2 and comic formats without conversion, plus PocketBook Cloud, Dropbox and Send-to-PocketBook for getting files on.

economical.note: PocketBook's German store lists the PocketBook Era Color at 239 euros including VAT.

products.name: PocketBook InkPad 4
products.description: A large 7.8-inch PocketBook for PDFs and bigger text.

openness.note: The InkPad 4 spec page lists the same 21 native book formats as the rest of the range, including Adobe DRM EPUB and PDF, used for library loans through Adobe Digital Editions.

economical.note: PocketBook's German store lists the PocketBook InkPad 4 at 289 euros including VAT.

products.name: PocketBook InkPad Color 3
products.description: PocketBook's large colour reader, also reading DRM-free Kindle AZW files.

openness.note: PocketBook's InkPad Color 3 spec lists EPUB and PDF with Adobe DRM, DRM-free AZW and AZW3, MOBI, DJVU and comics among formats read without conversion.

economical.note: PocketBook's German store lists the PocketBook InkPad Color 3 at 329 euros including VAT.

products.name: BOOX Note Air5 C
products.description: A 10.3-inch colour e-ink Android tablet that runs any reading app, including Kindle, Kobo and Libby; registered in the EU as a tablet.

openness.note: BOOX says the Note Air5 C runs Android 15 'With access to the Google Play Store', so Kindle, Kobo, Libby and other reading apps install alongside its own reader for EPUB and PDF.

longevity.note: Because it runs Android, the Note Air5 C has an EU tablet label record (EPREL 2496171): BOOX declares at least 7 years of updates after the model leaves the EU market, a repairability index of 3.97 out of 5 (class B) and a battery rated for 1,000 cycles.

economical.note: BOOX's US store lists the Note Air5 C at US$469.99 on the product page on the date checked.

products.name: BOOX Go 10.3 (Gen II)
products.description: A slim 10.3-inch black-and-white e-ink Android tablet for reading and notes, open to any app store reading app.

openness.note: BOOX says the Go 10.3 (Gen II) supports 26 digital formats including EPUB, PDF and AZW3 and gives access to apps 'via the Google Play Store', so library and store apps from several shops can be used.

longevity.note: The Go 10.3 (Gen II) EU tablet label record (EPREL 2666434) declares at least 5 years of updates after the model leaves the EU market, repairability index 3.01 (class C) and a battery rated for 1,000 cycles.

economical.note: BOOX's US store lists the Go 10.3 (Gen II) from US$399.99.
